title: A Ember for the Wolf
premise: When the border wards collapse and the stars vanish, Odile Winterbourne learns she is the last living signatory of the Ember Covenant, a pact her guild secretly forged between the human city of Vael and the wolf-kin of the northern wilds. Hunted by the Crown's Wardens and guided by a wolf-kin exile named Renn who remembers her from a life she cannot recall, Odile must recover the scattered embers of the covenant before the thirteenth moon turns. Each ember restores a fragment of her erased memory, revealing that she chose to forget the man she loved and the duty that broke them. In the end, Odile reforges the covenant not by restoring what was, but by writing a new pact with her own blood—sacrificing her memories of Renn so the two realms can see each other clearly at last.
about_author: W. M. Oyelaran is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing folk charms in West African and Celtic oral traditions before turning to fiction. They write quiet, memory-haunted fantasy about people who carry more history than they know.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Selling charms in Vael's night market, Odile feels her wards fail as every star vanishes at once. The emotional beat is dread beneath routine—the moment invisibility stops working.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Small Magic
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Flashback woven through present: how she joined the dying Charmwrights' Guild and learned to stay small. Beat: longing for a life she can't name.

chapters.title: The Warden at the Door
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A Crown Warden named Halvard questions her about illegal magic; she lies well but notices he carries an ember-glass pendant. Beat: fear sharpening into suspicion.

chapters.title: What Fell From the Border
chapters.summary: Renn's POV. A wolf-kin exile crosses the fallen wards into Vael, wounded and carrying a shard of covenant-stone that hums when Odile passes. Beat: recognition without understanding.

chapters.title: The Shard That Knows My Name
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The shard burns her palm and floods her with a single image: standing on a wall beside someone whose face is blurred. Beat: vertigo of stolen memory.

chapters.title: A Wolf in the Cellar
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She hides the injured Renn beneath her shop, trading barbs with him while treating his wounds. Beat: reluctant trust kindling.

chapters.title: The Guild's Last Ledger
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. In the ruined guildhall she finds a ledger listing thirteen embers—and her own name as final signatory, dated twelve years ago. Beat: identity cracking open.

chapters.title: Halvard Closes the Net
chapters.summary: Halvard's POV. The Warden traces illegal charm-signatures to Odile's street, torn between duty and doubt. Beat: antagonist given a conscience.

chapters.title: Flight Through the Ash Market
chapters.summary: Odile and Renn's alternating POV. Wardens raid the market; Renn reveals his wolf form to save her, exposing them both. Beat: point of no return.

chapters.title: The Road North
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Fleeing the city walls, Odile learns the first ember lies in a drowned chapel beyond the marshes. Beat: grim resolve replacing fear.

chapters.title: The Drowned Chapel
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Retrieving the first ember triggers a full memory: she stood on the border wall at nineteen, swearing an oath beside a man she still cannot see. Beat: grief for an unknown loss.

chapters.title: What Renn Won't Say
chapters.summary: Renn's POV. Renn recognizes Odile but conceals their shared past, fearing the truth will break her before the moons turn. Beat: love expressed as silence.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Moon Rises
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. An astronomer exile explains the deadline: when the hidden moon completes its cycle, the realms drift apart forever. Beat: stakes made cosmic and personal.

chapters.title: Wolves at the Ford
chapters.summary: Shared POV. A wild pack confronts them; Renn negotiates passage by submitting to a humiliating rite. Beat: cost of loyalty, Odile seeing Renn truly for the first time.

chapters.title: The Ember in the Bone Orchard
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The second ember is buried with the covenant's dead; claiming it shows Odile her own funeral procession—a death she apparently survived. Beat: uncanny horror softening into wonder.

chapters.title: Halvard's Bargain
chapters.summary: Halvard's POV. Offered promotion for Odile's capture, Halvard instead requests access to sealed guild archives. Beat: the hunter becoming a seeker.

chapters.title: The City That Forgot
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Passing through a village erased from maps, Odile realizes the Crown has been unmaking magic-touched places for decades. Beat: righteous anger.

chapters.title: Two Travelers, One Blanket
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A quiet campfire chapter: near-confessions interrupted by old wounds, both retreating. Beat: tenderness held at arm's length.

chapters.title: The Ember-Taker
chapters.summary: Renn's POV. A rival claimant—a disgraced guildmaster who betrayed the covenant—ambushes them and steals one ember. Beat: betrayal made flesh; personal stakes ignite.

chapters.title: The Guildmaster's Confession
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Captured briefly by the guildmaster, Odile hears how he sold the covenant and why her memories were taken: she asked for it. Beat: devastating revelation.

chapters.title: I Chose to Forget
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Alone after escaping, Odile reckons with the truth—she erased her own love to survive the covenant's breaking. Beat: rock-bottom despair.

chapters.title: Renn, Unmasked
chapters.summary: Renn's POV. Renn finally tells her: he was the man on the wall, her betrothed across realms, and he has spent twelve years searching. Beat: heartbreak and relief entwined.

chapters.title: The Third Ember and the Price of Knowing
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Recovering the stolen ember costs Renn a grave wound. Beat: love proven through sacrifice, guilt consuming Odile.

chapters.title: The Healer of Hollow Vale
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A hedge-healer saves Renn using outlawed magic, showing Odile a gentler model of power than the covenant's hard bargains. Beat: hope rekindled.

chapters.title: Halvard Finds Them
chapters.summary: Halvard's POV. Halvard corners them—but having read the archives, he offers instead to look away if they can prove the Crown was built on theft. Beat: uneasy alliance.

chapters.title: The Archive Beneath the Palace
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Infiltrating Vael, they find proof the founding kings stole the covenant's terms wholesale. Beat: the enemy reframed as system, not person.

chapters.title: Embers Four Through Seven
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A montage-like chapter of recovery across the realm, each ember returning memories both sweet and damning. Beat: wholeness arriving with pain attached.

chapters.title: The Queen Who Signed in Blood
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The eighth ember reveals Vael's queen once loved a wolf-kin and signed the original pact in secret. Beat: history rhyming with the present.

chapters.title: Moonrise Over the Wall
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Odile and Renn revisit the border wall where they first met; almost-love confessed fully now. Beat: the romance consummated emotionally, not physically.

chapters.title: The Betrayer's Last Ember
chapters.summary: Shared POV. The guildmaster, dying, returns the ninth ember and begs forgiveness; Odile refuses absolution but takes the ember. Beat: mercy without reconciliation.

chapters.title: Ten Moons Gone
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Time check: three turns remain, four embers left, and the Crown mobilizes to seal the border permanently. Beat: accelerating clock.

chapters.title: The Ember Beneath the Ice
chapters.summary: Shared POV. A perilous descent into a glacier vault claims supplies and nearly claims Renn again. Beat: endurance; partnership forged under pressure.

chapters.title: Halvard Stands Guard
chapters.summary: Halvard's POV. Halvard holds a pass against his own soldiers to buy the pair time, knowing it ends his career. Beat: redemption arc paying off.

chapters.title: The Twelfth Ember's Lie
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The twelfth ember reveals the covenant demands a memory-sacrifice from its reforged signer—she knows now what reforging will cost. Beat: anticipatory grief.

chapters.title: One Turn Left
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A still night before the endgame: Renn promises to remember for both of them. Beat: quiet devastation, love accepting loss.

chapters.title: The Gathering at the Border
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Wolves, outlaws, Halvard's defectors, and common folk converge on the wall as the final moon wanes. Beat: hope massing against odds.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. At the wall's heart, Odile writes the new covenant in her blood, offering her memories of Renn as the price. Beat: climax—choice made with open eyes.

chapters.title: Thirteen Moons Full
chapters.summary: Renn's POV. As stars return, Renn watches Odile look at him with kind, total strangeness—and keeps his promise to remember enough for both. Beat: bittersweet triumph.

chapters.title: The Charm Shop Reopens
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Months later, Odile runs a legal charm shop between two reconciled realms, drawn to a gray-eyed customer she feels she's met in dreams. Beat: gentle ache, identity remade.

chapters.title: An Ember Kept Burning
chapters.summary: Dual closing POV. Renn begins telling her their story from the beginning; the last line mirrors the book's first. Beat: resolution—love as a story told again until remembered.
